chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man urinates and does not have water with him, so he wipes his penis on the wall. He said: “Everything dry is pure.”
As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who performs wudu (ablution) and forgets to wash his penis, he said: “He washes his penis, then repeats the wudu (ablution).” This is to be understood as recommendation and desirability, as indicated by the previous reports, and because contradiction between the reports and statements of the Imams عليهم السلام is not permissible.

As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr al-Bajalī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, who said: I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying:

“If a man forgot to perform istinjaʾ after defecation until he prayed, he does not repeat the salat (prayer).” Its meaning is that he forgot to perform istinjaʾ with water, not that he forgot istinjaʾ in every respect, because if he performed istinjaʾ with a stone, that suffices him in place of water. What has previously been mentioned of the reports indicates this and further confirms it.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; indicating a non-obligatory but encouraged ruling
key_terms.الْحَجَرِ: stone; used here as a valid means of istinjaʾ
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: feces; excrement after which cleansing is discussed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution); the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.ذَكَرَهُ: his penis; the male private organ discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: pure; clean in the legal sense in this context
key_terms.يَابِسٍ: dry; referring here to dryness as affecting the state of impurity
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinjaʾ; to cleanse oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Does forgetting to wash after urination or defecation invalidate wudu (ablution) or salat (prayer) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings related to ritual purity after relieving oneself and the effect of dryness in removing impurity. It also reconciles narrations concerning washing the private part and repeating wudu (ablution), clarifying that some reports are understood as recommending repetition rather than making it obligatory.
